subject: GCP private basket: special pricing & rev-share carveout — exec clearance needed
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@datanimbus.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 Sep 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Request: GCP Private basket + marketplace listing (pricing/terms)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at DataNimbus is excited about adopting Redwood for our inference inference tier on GCP. Procurement asked me to put the ask in writing to speed things up.

High-level: we need a GCP Private Offer (Marketplace) for an immediate pilot with the option to scale to a committed 12-month footprint. Two items are blocking procurement:

- Pricing: to get the pilot budgeted we need a 40% discount on list for the first 3 months (pilot), then 25% for months 4–12.
- Rev-share / marketplace carveout: GCP requires a slightly different split for usage billed in the marketplace. We need the marketplace rev-share to be 35% to GCP, and we would like Redwood to accept a 65/35 rev-share in your favor for the first 12 months (i.e., Redwood retains 65%). This is nonstandard versus what we saw in your docs — procurement called this out as "carveout request."

Also procurement attached their standard questionnaire (sent as a separate attachment).

Can you confirm if Redwood can support these terms or what approvals are required? We have to hit procurement board on Monday.

Appreciate the quick turnaround,
Olivia
Olivia Chen
Head of Cloud Partnerships, DataNimbus AI
olivia.chen@datanimbus.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: Procurement_QA_Datanimbus.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@datanimbus.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 Sep 2028 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: GCP Private basket + marketplace listing (pricing/terms)

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear ask and sending the procurement questionnaire.

Short answer: we can move forward but the discount and rev-share carveout are outside standard delegated authority. I need to loop in pricing/legal/ops for rev-share alignment and get executive clearance for the pilot discount cadence you requested (40% then 25%).

I attached a draft private offer (v3) with our typical marketplace split and the redline fields highlighted (pricing, rev-share, billing terms). To make Monday realistic, can you confirm:
- whether DataNimbus needs net-60 payment terms for Redwood invoiced amounts (procurement ticked Net-60)
- if the pilot start date has any hard dependency on GCP listing timeline (we can do a private offer pre-listing if needed)

I'll escalate internally now and share internal notes back to you by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Account Executive — Cloud Marketplaces
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
(650) 555-0223

Attachments: Datanimbus_GCP_Private_Offer_v3.pdf, redwood_priv_offer_terms_redline.docx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 8 Sep 2028 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec clearance request — DataNimbus GCP private offer (DN-2028-GCP-0173)

Team —

We have a commercial ask from DataNimbus that needs exec/finance signoff ahead of Monday procurement meeting. Summary:
- Customer: DataNimbus AI (startup, HC to pilot production)
- Ask: Pilot pricing 40% off list for months 0–3, then 25% months 4–12; request to accept net-60 invoicing; marketplace rev-share carveout requested to result in Redwood retaining 65% (i.e., a GCP cut of 35% that the customer expects to be baked into the private offer split).
- Why nonstandard: our default marketplace split is 20% platform (approx) to marketplace; the requested GCP split and the staged discount cadence materially impact our unit economics for the first 12 months.
- Documents attached: private offer v3 with highlighted redlines, procurement QA.

Recommendation from AE: if we cap total effective discount (after factoring rev-share impact) at ~33% effective for months 0–3 and 20% thereafter, we can accept the staged discounts, but we need finance signoff for net-60 and an explicit rev-share carveout approval from Marketplace Ops.

Questions for approvers:
1) Marissa — do you approve pushing this to Exec for a >30% effective discount?
2) Vivek — do we have precedent for agreeing to net-60 on private offers with startups at this stage?
3) Laura / Legal — any red flags in the redline on term alignment (rollback, indemnities, data residency clause in procurement QA)?

We need a binary decision by tomorrow EOD to get DocuSign and the HubSpot close moved before procurement review.

Thanks,
Karthik

Attachment: Datanimbus_GCP_Private_Offer_v3.pdf (pdf), procurement_QA_datanimbus.xlsx (xlsx), redwood_priv_offer_terms_redline.docx (docx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 8 Sep 2028 16:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exec clearance request — DataNimbus GCP private offer (DN-2028-GCP-0173)

Karthik / team —

Thanks for the context and the clear recommendation. My position:
- I can approve up to an effective 30% discount for months 0–3 (after accounting for marketplace take). Anything above 30% effective requires CFO approval. 40% list up front is higher than our playbook for pilot deals unless there is a clear committed upsell path (which the AE notes; still needs risk quantification).
- Net-60: acceptable only if Finance signs off on a credit hold / escrow option tied to contract milestones. We should not accept open net-60 without mitigation.
- Rev-share carveout: this needs a Marketplace Ops exception; I authorize the escalation to ops but we should require GCP fee transparency and a clause that the rev-share alignment is timeboxed to the 12-month pilot period.

Action items I want executed before any signature:
1) Finance to confirm mechanism for risk mitigation for Net-60 (Laura / Jordan, can you work with Finance and draft the escrow clause?)
2) Ops to review rev-share carveout (Jordan, can you open an ops ticket and loop in the marketplace partner manager?)
3) AE to update HubSpot with a conditional offer (link to deal) and set a Monday procurement meeting reminder.

If we get those in place, I will sign off on an up-to-30% effective discount and time-limited rev-share acceptance.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Cloud Marketplaces
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Forwarded-For-Visibility: Vivek — if you can give final signoff scope (CRO / CFO) I'll route DocuSign afterwards.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 9 Sep 2028 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exec clearance request — DataNimbus GCP private offer (DN-2028-GCP-0173)

Team — after reviewing the financial impact and the mitigation plan Marissa and Jordan outlined, I approve the following (final signoff):

- Discount: Approve up to 30% effective discount for months 0–3, then 20% months 4–12. We will not approve 40% list up front.
- Rev-share carveout: Approve a timeboxed rev-share alignment for 12 months provided Marketplace Ops confirms GCP takes <=35% and that the carveout is documented in the private offer language (and rolls to standard split thereafter).
- Net terms: Approve net-60 only with a performance-based escrow / milestone payment schedule; Finance to draft clause and Finance lead must be cc'd on DocuSign.

Please update HubSpot (deal DN-2028-GCP-0173) to reflect conditional approval and prepare a DocuSign with the agreed redlines. Jordan — open Ops ticket with priority-high and include marketplace partner manager (cc: partner_ops@gcp-partners.example).

Once the above items are in the package, AE can present to DataNimbus procurement and we can sign.

Vivek Kulkarni
Chief Revenue Officer
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Note: Deal ID DN-2028-GCP-0173. Marking as approved-with-conditions.
